subject: geography
title: Earth’s structure and plate tectonics
objective: Explain how moving plates shape the surface.

lesson.opening: Earth’s outer shell is broken into plates that move slowly over the hot interior, building mountains, oceans, and volcanoes where they meet.

sections.heading: Inside the Earth
sections.body: A thin rocky crust sits on the mantle, with a dense metal core at the centre. Heat from the interior drives slow motion in the mantle.

sections.heading: Three boundaries
sections.body: At divergent boundaries plates pull apart and new crust forms. At convergent boundaries plates collide, lifting mountains or sinking into trenches. At transform boundaries they slide past each other, causing earthquakes.

sections.heading: The Ring of Fire
sections.body: Most of the world’s volcanoes and large earthquakes trace plate edges, especially around the Pacific.

activities.prompt: Mountains such as the Himalayas form mainly at a…
Earthquakes at a transform boundary are caused by plates…
The Ring of Fire is a belt of…
choices: Volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific

activities.prompt: Explain how one type of plate boundary creates a landform.
activities.instructions: Name the boundary and the feature.
activities.context: Convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries each produce distinctive features.
